    13	  \ THAT MUST NOT BE BLURRED, and it is why the freeness next door does not help here:

    17	  \ object is NOT, and it is what JacobianData needs. For the
   class-indexed atlas\
    18	  \ the index type is infinite, so the finite route JacobianData.ofCharts
   ([Finite\
    19	  \ iota] + per-chart compactness) IS UNAVAILABLE, and ofChartsOfCompactSpace takes\
    20	  \ the
   glued compactness directly.
Anyone quoting "compactness is free at the\

conflation this note exists\
    22	  \ to prevent. ajcr-p4 stated the distinction correctly in their own file;
keep\

does\

DAT-J: JacobianData assembly -- quasi-compactness via the Abel image\
    30	  \ of Div^g-lite.

*** CORRECTION AT THE TOP, 2026-07-29 (run 0071 s0016 close,\
    31	  \ ajcr-divrep), against MY OWN header
below. A fresh-context audit (I-0799/I-0800/I-0802/I-0803)\
    32	  \ refuted three of its claims. Commit
9753ad6e3; the Lean is unchanged and still\
    33	  \ kernel-green, the PRICING was wrong.

WHAT SURVIVES: the effectivity half is\
    34	  \ genuinely divRep-FREE (the audit cone-checked 323 files:
no divRepClassify, no\
    35	  \ DivRepAffinePullback, no IsChartClause, no universal family), and the three
\
    36	  theorems are real, sorry-free, rooted and axiom-clean.

WHAT IS REFUTED -- and\
    37	  \ it is the word "discharged":
 (1) I called exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero\
    38	  \ a SATISFIABILITY PROBE and claimed the
     degree map hits g "unconditionally\
    39	  \ on the curve". FALSE, arithmetically: CurveDivisor.deg is
     weighted by residue\
    40	  \ degrees (Divisor.lean:61), so its image is index*Z. On a genus-1 curve of
  \
    41	  \   index 3 over Q no divisor of degree 1 = g exists and the theorem is a VACUOUS\
    42	  \ TRUTH. The
     campaign reference does not escape it: deg (m . fiberWeilDivisor)\
    43	  \ = m*delta (WindowLedger:133)
     requires delta | g. So the face RELOCATES the\
    44	  \ hypothesis (Z is an ARGUMENT), it does not
     discharge it. Exactly the reduction-to-a-possibly-false-hypothesis\
    45	  \ trap this project has
     recorded twice -- passes every census because it IS\
    46	  \ then a theorem.
 (2) THE BINDING LIMIT IS NOT THE DESCENT ONE I DISCLOSED. Since\
    47	  \ the splitting field L is
     existential inside the proof, the reference binder\
    48	  \ is UNIFORM: forall L, deg L (Zof L) = g,
     over every extension including\
    49	  \ L = k. Strictly stronger than the degree-0 face asks, and it
     has NO PRODUCER\
    50	  \ anywhere in the tree.
 (3) THE CONE IS NOT Challenge-FREE, which w4-datj 0.5/3.4\
    51	  \ make BINDING for a DAT-J producer:
     DivisorDatumRankOne -> Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance:6\
    52	  \ -> Challenge. So "available today"
     does NOT mean "consumable by DJ-2/DJ-3\
    53	  \ today". Separately: 0.5's own claim that FLVClass is
     Challenge-free is\
    54	  \ also false at HEAD (Degree.lean:7 -> ChiCurve -> Challenge), so the standing
\
    55	  \     "never riemann_inequality_curve" rule no longer avoids the cycle. Tree-wide,\
    56	  \ pre-existing,
     and it needs its own decision.
 (4) A docstring advertised\
    57	  \ PicRepDatum.exists_effective_deg_eq_at_point, which DOES NOT EXIST.
     So the\
    58	  \ one face that would consume the Pic^0 universal property is absent; lam/hlam remain
\
    59	  \     caller-supplied.

SO THE HONEST STATE OF THE EFFECTIVITY HALF: divRep-free,\
    60	  \ and CONDITIONAL on an arithmetic
hypothesis about the curve's index that nothing\
    61	  \ produces. Not discharged.

WHAT DAT-J OWES NOW: (a) a degree-g divisor over\
    62	  \ the relevant field -- an index condition, newly
visible and genuinely open; (b)\
    63	  \ descent from the splitting field to kappa(y) (dat-g); (c) the Abel
square at\
    64	  \ an INDEPENDENTLY PINNED pt (the s0012 retraction stands); (d) a PicRepDatum from\
    65	  \ DAT-G
(divRep-gated); (e) a Challenge-free route for the whole producer cone.\
    66	  \ DJ-0 remains landed.

DAT-J: JacobianData assembly\
    68	  \ -- quasi-compactness via the Abel image of Div^g-lite.

*** THE EFFECTIVITY\
    69	  \ HALF IS DISCHARGED AND WAS NEVER divRep-GATED, 2026-07-29 (run 0071 s0016,
ajcr-divrep).\
    70	  \ Commits 053897f16 + c8a4563af + 127d7cccf; kernel EXIT=0, axiom-clean against\
    71	  \ a
control reporting sorryAx; root build 9288 jobs EXIT=0.

  exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq\
    72	  \ (Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean)
    with chi(O) = 1 - g, a Cech Picard\
    73	  \ class of degree g has an EFFECTIVE representative OF
    DEGREE g.  General:\
    74	  \ any X, no relative curve, no pi.
  exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero
\
    75	  \    the satisfiability face AND the usable one -- a degree-ZERO class times a degree-g
\
    76	  \    reference divisor.  The classes this row actually holds are of degree zero.
\
    77	  \  exists_effective_deg_eq_of_pic0_at_point (Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffectivePoint.lean)
\
    78	  \    from a point y of ANY Pic^0-representing object: a finite separable L over\
    79	  \ kappa(y) and an
    effective degree-g divisor over L presenting the restricted\
    80	  \ class.

THE GAP WAS ONE CONJUNCT, AND IT WAS A STATEMENT GAP. Every effectivity\
    81	  \ lemma in the tree stops
at "0 <= E and picClass E = picClass W" with NO claim\
    82	  \ about deg E (exists_effective_of_picClass
FLVClass:208, exists_effective_of_h0_pos\
    83	  \ SectionBound:175), while effectiveDivisorClassifyZar
(DivisorFamilyFieldSurj:217)\
    84	  \ demands 0 <= D AND deg D = g. Degree is a class invariant
(deg_eq_deg_of_picClass_eq),\
    85	  \ so the missing conjunct transports for free off the class equation.

TWO COST\
    86	  \ CLAIMS RETRACTED AT THEIR OWN SITES (not merely superseded here):
 * JacobianDataAbelImage\
    87	  \ said DJ-1's brick "needs the universal degree-g class, hence divRep".
   It\
    88	  \ does not. The five steps from a POINT to a divisor are all landed and all divRep-free:
\
    89	  \   Over.testPoint (Pic0ChartTestPoint:176), mem_pic0Subgroup_iff, exists_splitting_of_picEt
\
    90	  \   (Pic0ChartSplit:143, UNCONDITIONAL on the curve), classDeg_presenting_eq_zero
\
    91	  \   (Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2:98), then the brick.
 * The same docstring predicted\
    92	  \ a fiberTwist shift. NONE is needed: at degree exactly g the RR
   entry condition\
    93	  \ 1 <= deg W + chi(O) reads g <= deg W, so the class sits ON THE BOUNDARY and
\
    94	  \   fires with no slack.

SO THE TWO HALVES OF STEP 3 WERE NEVER GATED ALIKE,\
    95	  \ and this row priced them together -- hiding
a discharged half behind a gated\
    96	  \ one. Only the Abel SQUARE is divRep-gated, because naming abel
at all requires\
    97	  \ the representation.

WHAT REMAINS, exactly:
 (1) DESCENT, the honest new residue:\
    98	  \ the divisor lives over the finite separable SPLITTING
     field L, while hlift\
    99	  \ wants a morphism out of Spec kappa(y). That is dat-g's work.
 (2) the Abel-compatibility\
   100	  \ square at a pt PINNED INDEPENDENTLY (the s0012 retraction below
     stands:\
   101	  \ at a chosen pt the split is vacuous and its consumer is circular).
 (3) a PicRepDatum\
   102	  \ k k C from DAT-G (divRep-gated).
 (4) the caller's degree-g reference divisor\
   103	  \ Z -- over a small finite field a real hypothesis,
     not bookkeeping.
DJ-0\
   104	  \ compact-image qc remains landed.

    for an ARBITRARY abel : DivScheme g --> J, SOME pt satisfies\

square is dif_pos.\
   114	  \ No geometry, no surjectivity, no property of abel whatsoever.

IsAbelClassifyCompatible,\
   116	  \ not fixed campaign data. A consumer entitled to choose pt can choose
the classifier\
   117	  \ composite itself. This row called item 1 "bookkeeping-shaped, but a real
statement,\
   118	  \ and nobody has written it" -- it is not a statement about abel at all. Recorded
\
   119	  shape: I-0605 (a residue existentially quantified over the datum that would give\
   120	  \ it content
demands nothing; inhabit it with junk BEFORE pricing it).

AND THE\

  heff_iff_conclusion_of_pt_eq\
   122	  \ (same file)
At that pt, the remaining hypothesis heff of exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible
\
   123	  (JacobianDataAbelSquare.lean:158) unfolds to VERBATIM its own conclusion, so that\
   124	  \ theorem is a
tautology there. heff had silently absorbed all the content item\
   125	  \ 1 appeared to carry. So
exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible is a reduction\
   126	  \ only RELATIVE TO A pt PINNED
INDEPENDENTLY -- pinned to the campaign Abel map's\
   127	  \ own point map -- and the interface never
pins it.

WHAT DAT-J NOW OWES, exactly\
   128	  \ one statement:
  for every point y of J, an effective degree-g divisor D on the\
   129	  \ curve over kappa(y) WHOSE
  CLASSIFYING MORPHISM COMPOSES WITH abel TO fromSpecResidueField\
   130	  \ y.
The Riemann-Roch half produces D; the compatibility half is the honest residue.\
   131	  \ The split into
"the square" plus "the geometry" CANNOT be restored: any pt\
   132	  \ making the split statable is either
the pinned campaign one (in which case there\
   133	  \ is no separate row) or a chosen one (in which case
the split is vacuous). Spelling\
   134	  \ of the RR half stays BINDING per w4-datj 0.5:
exists_effective_of_picClass /\
   135	  \ riemann_inequality (FLVClass.lean:208/205), NEVER
riemann_inequality_curve (ChiCurve.lean:183,\
   136	  \ imports Challenge.lean -- import cycle).

STILL OPEN AND UNCHANGED: a PicRepDatum\
   137	  \ k k C from DAT-G (divRep-gated).

--- the pre-retraction body follows; item\
   138	  \ 1 of its "owes" list is now REFUTED, item 2 is
--- restated above as the single\
   139	  \ obligation, item 3 stands ---

STATUS 2026-07-28 (run 0071 s0008, ajcr-divrep).\
   140	  \ STEP 3 IS A COMPATIBILITY SQUARE, NOT A
CONSTRUCTION -- because the fibrewise\

THE STRATEGIC POINT, and it is the sharp form of critical-path\

DivFamZar no-go is a purely RELATIVE phenomenon (over\

many closed points, so IsPreconnected\
   149	  \ supportLocus is vacuous). The certificate difficulty that
makes U2 hard DOES\
   150	  \ NOT EXIST FIBREWISE. Any obligation phrased over a residue field should be
priced\
   151	  \ against DivisorFamilyFieldSurj, not against the relative certificate machinery.
\

DJ-0 (compact-image qc) and DJ-2 (packaging) remain landed. JacobianData has seven\

plus the two PicRepDatum entry points; the atlas is NOT finite, so\

 \section{The Jacobian as an abelian variety}
 
 \begin{definition}[Jacobian]
-  \label{def:jacobian}
-  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian}
+ \label{def:jacobian}
+ \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian}
+ \uses{def:pic0Functor}
+ \source{kleiman-picard}
   The \emph{Jacobian} \(\Jac(C)\) of a smooth proper curve \(C\) over \(k\) is the identity
   component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) of the relative Picard scheme of \(C\) over \(k\): the \(k\)-scheme

+  representing the degree-zero subfunctor of the \'etale-sheafified relative Picard functor.
 \end{definition}
 
 \begin{proposition}[Group scheme structure]
@@ -93,7 +95,11 @@ In particular \(\Jac(C)\) is an abelian variety over \(k\) of dimension \(g(C)\)

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.EffectiveUniqueness

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ThetaDegree

/-!
# The target degree is a WINDOW, not the genus — and at `deg = g` the two chart conditions coincide

`Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean` proves that a class of degree **exactly** `g` on a
curve with `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g` has an effective representative of degree `g`, and its
`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero` docstring carries a retraction that ends:

> "**So what this lemma does is RELOCATE the hypothesis, not discharge it** — `Z` is an
> argument. […] Producing `Z` is a genuine arithmetic hypothesis on the curve, open here."

That retraction is **correct about `= g` and wrong about the obligation**, and this file
separates the two.  The arithmetic obstruction it records is real: `CurveDivisor.deg` is
weighted by residue degrees (`RiemannRoch/Divisor.lean`), so its image is `index · ℤ`, and on
a curve of index `3` and genus `1` there is no divisor of degree `1 = g`.  But that
obstruction is an artefact of the **equality**.  Read the proof of
`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq`: the hypothesis `classDeg K L = g` is used twice, and
in one of the two places only `g ≤ classDeg K L` is needed —

* to enter Riemann's inequality, via `1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪) = deg W + 1 − g`, i.e. `g ≤ deg W`;
* to *state* the conclusion's degree, which is where the equality is genuinely consumed.

Decoupling them gives the same theorem over a **window** of target degrees, and then the
reference divisor is no longer an arithmetic hypothesis: the campaign's own
`m • fiberWeilDivisor π` has degree `m · δ` with `1 ≤ δ` (`deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ`,
`one_le_windowδ`), so `g ≤ deg` is reachable at `m := g` on **every** curve, while `= g`
needs `δ ∣ g`.

## The second half, and it is the one that changes another lane's plan

At the *representability* degree `deg = g` the two conditions the chart layer treats as
separate are the **same condition**.  With `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g` the rank anchor
`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`) reads

  `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = deg D + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1`,

so **`h¹ = 0` alone forces `h⁰ = 1`** for a degree-`g` divisor.  `h¹ = 0` is what coverage
asks for (`IsSplitWitness`, and `Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`'s drop-free membership);
`h⁰ = 1` is one of the four inputs of DAT-C GAP-2
(`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`).

**SCOPED, 2026-07-29, by a fresh-context review of this file, before anything consumed it.**
A first draft of this paragraph said coverage's hypothesis and GAP-2's hypothesis are "the same
hypothesis", and that the index-slack residue and coverage's drop-freeness are "two faces of one
identity".  **Both sentences were too strong and are withdrawn.**  `eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`
takes **four** inputs — `0 ≤ D`, `0 ≤ D'`, the class equation, and `h⁰ = 1` — and the identity
below substitutes only the last.  **Effectivity is passed through unchanged, and effectivity is
precisely what coverage does not carry**: `IsSplitWitness`'s own docstring
(`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:145-149`) says so, and warns in terms that apply exactly here that "a lane
that reads `IsSplitWitness` as already giving it will have a gap where it least expects one".
Dropping `0 ≤ D'` from the theorem below and closing with `exact?` fails.

What survives, and it is worth having but smaller: **GAP-2 goes from four inputs to three** at
degree `g`.  Two further scopings of record, both from the same review:

* the identity is *interderivable* with the already-landed `hb_forces_h0_eq_one`
  (`Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean:180`, the same one-line proof), and `IndexSlack:175` already
  headlines "the χ-ledger turns it into an `h⁰` equality" — so the χ-ledger reading is not new
  here, only packaged;
* `IndexSlack`'s reading of its own conclusion as a defect concerns the *universally quantified*
  form ("**every** degree-`g` divisor has `h⁰ = 1`", false with a moving degree-`g` family).  The
  pointwise form below is not a defect.  That distinction stands; the claim that it *unifies* the
  two findings does not.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effective_deg_eq_of_le_classDeg` — the window form: for **any**
  target degree `d` with `g ≤ d`, a class of degree `d` has an effective representative of
  degree `d`.  Strictly generalises `exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq` (`d := g`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_le_deg` — the degree-zero face
  with the reference divisor's degree only **bounded below**, which is what removes the
  arithmetic hypothesis.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_reference_divisor_le_deg` — and the reference divisor at that
  bound **exists on every curve of the campaign bundle**, so the face above is inhabited rather
  than conditional.  **It does NOT discharge the retraction's "open here"** — a first draft said
  it did, and that was withdrawn by a fresh-context review of this file: the conclusion weakened
  in lockstep with the hypothesis, so the divisibility obstruction moved from the *input* degree
  to the *output* degree rather than dissolving.  See the honest-limit paragraph on
  `exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_toP1`, and the review's own generalisation of the
  pattern (a weakened hypothesis can look like a discharged obstruction when it only relocated
  the same obstruction to the output).  The `π` in this statement is also **not load-bearing**:
  the section's `[LocallyOfFiniteType]` already gives `Scheme.residueDeg_pos`, so `d` copies of
  any non-generic point prove the identical conclusion with no `ℙ¹` anywhere.  `π` is kept
  because it is the datum the campaign's curve actually carries.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_eq` — the identity: at
  degree `g` with `χ = 1 − g`, `h¹ = 0` forces `h⁰ = 1`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_deg_eq_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` — GAP-2's
  uniqueness conclusion from the **coverage** hypothesis, with no `h⁰` input at all.

## What this does NOT do

It does not produce a chart, does not discharge `IsChartUniv`, and does not produce the
local-surjectivity instance.  It removes one arithmetic hypothesis from the effectivity leg
and identifies two chart-layer conditions at the representability degree.  The `V`-coupling
(I-0861, I-0869) and the `exists_factor` field are untouched and remain open.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

        rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_nsmul' K]

/-- **The effectivity leg with NO arithmetic hypothesis left**: on a curve with a finite
dominant map to `ℙ¹`, every degree-zero class has an effective representative, of some degree
`≥ g` named by the statement.

This composes `exists_reference_divisor_le_deg` with
`exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_le_deg`.  Compare
`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero`, which takes the reference divisor as an argument
and whose docstring records producing it as "a genuine arithmetic hypothesis on the curve, open
here": here nothing is assumed about the curve beyond the package it already carries.

What is *given up* relative to the `= g` form, stated plainly because it is the honest cost:
the resulting degree is `deg Z`, a multiple of `δ` at least `g`, not `g` on the nose.  A
consumer that genuinely needs degree exactly `g` — `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar`
(`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean`) does, through its `hdeg` field — is **not** served by
this, and that residue is unchanged.  What this settles is that the obstruction lives in the
*consumer's* degree pin, not in the curve's arithmetic. -/
theorem exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_toP1 (g : ℕ)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsDominant π] [IsFinite π]
    (L₀ : Y.CechPic) (hL₀ : classDeg K L₀ = 0) :
    ∃ (Z : Y.CurveDivisor) (E : Y.CurveDivisor), (g : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K Z ∧
      0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = L₀ * CurveDivisor.picClass K Z ∧
      CurveDivisor.deg K E = CurveDivisor.deg K Z := by
  obtain ⟨Z, hZ⟩ := exists_reference_divisor_le_deg K π g
  obtain ⟨E, hE, hcl, hdeg⟩ :=
    exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_le_deg K g hχ Z hZ L₀ hL₀
  exact ⟨Z, E, hZ, hE, hcl, hdeg⟩

end Reference

(JacobianData.ofCharts with per-chart compactness at an empty cover), with coverage contributing
nothing. A degenerate index attributes to whichever hypothesis happens to vary, and I varied the
wrong one.

(glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace fails on EXACTLY ONE goal --
Finite (glueData hf).openCover.I0. Not chart compactness, not the cover being a cover, not
coverage. Add [Finite iota] plus per-chart CompactSpace and the same term closes. p4 also applies my
own I-0978 correctly: a failing synthesis measures the instance graph, so this does NOT prove hcpt
independent of coverage -- it shows no route in scope derives it, and the single gap on the
available route is INDEX FINITENESS, which the class-indexed atlas provably lacks.

At genus zero, hvan and the fibrewise rigidity predicate are equivalent spellings. The rigid engine and the unit-equation lemma are genuine, sorry-free infrastructure, but hrigAff still has no producer over a general non-field test algebra.
